# 02 geo_index_core -- perf (plan 02 P.1 / P.2)

MEASURED 2026-11-19T17:15Z on c05: Docker `geo-index-core` (ubuntu 24.04, libs2-dev 0.10.0, libbenchmark 1.8.3),
`--cpuset-cpus=20-23`, Release (-O3), 32 host CPUs @ 2445 MHz.  Google Benchmark,
3 repetitions, median CPU time.  Reproduce: `docker run --rm -v $PWD/contrib/geo_index_core:/src geo-index-core /src/run_bench.sh`.
(`library_build_type: debug` in the JSON is libbenchmark's own Ubuntu build flag, not our code.)

## Findings -> P.2 decisions
1. **Drop Expand.**  It never helped: plan 02 A.4 found 0 false negatives without it (273,621 inside + 48,416
   boundary points).  It costs +8-20% CPU in cover() and +18-42% candidates (city at max_cells 64: 124 -> 163).
   R-KISS: remove it; the A.4 property tests stay as the guard.
2. **Default max_cells = 64.**  It is the largest setting under the 1 ms budget for every polygon (0.39-0.67 ms).
   256 tightens selectivity (city 1.38 -> 1.14) but costs 1.5-2.3 ms per query; that only pays off when
   the 24% fewer candidate rows take more than ~1.5 ms to scan, i.e. on large tables.  kiss: fixed 64;
   upgrade when plan 01 Z.3 Profile shows cover false positives > 20% of scanned rows.
3. **Default column level = 16** (S2 level-16 cell ~ 150 m edge).  At max_cells 64, levels 12/16/20 give the
   same ranges and candidates, so level only sets the floor for later, finer covers.  16 keeps that floor
   at street-block size.
4. **Two shapes miss the 2x candidate/hit bar at 64 cells**: `thin` (a 1.7 km-wide, 240 km-long diagonal
   sliver; 7.5x) and `pole_cap` (3.1x).  Both are bounded by cells, not by the algorithm: thin is 1.95x at
   1024 cells.  Accepted for G5 with the note: for a sliver the index still scans far fewer rows than the
   full scan (158 vs 9,491 fixture points here; plan 01 B.3 bbox did not help thin at all, 1.3x).
   The Doris-side recheck stays exact, so this costs speed only, never correctness.
5. cover() runs once per query on the FE-sent polygon: 0.4-0.7 ms is < 1% of the 62-227 ms baseline query
   time (01.geo.baseline.md).  Ranges at 64 cells: 11-42 -> the planner's `cell BETWEEN` list stays small.
